title: de Broglie wavelength
examples: What is the de Broglie equation?
How does momentum relate to wavelength?
Can you explain electron diffraction to me?

explain.say: Today we will learn about de Broglie wavelength. It shows particles act like waves.
The de Broglie equation is lambda equals h divided by p. This links wave and particle properties.
Momentum is mass times velocity. So p is m times v. This is a key relationship.
Electron diffraction shows this wave nature clearly. Electrons bend around crystals like waves do.
In a real lab experiment, scientists use crystals. They measure the angle of diffracted electrons. This confirms wave behavior.
A common mistake is forgetting to use SI units. Always check your units for mass and velocity.

items: Use meters per second for velocity.

faq.a: Planck's constant is a fundamental physical constant. It relates energy to frequency in quantum mechanics.
asks: What is the value of h?

faq.q: Does this only apply to electrons?
faq.a: No, the de Broglie hypothesis applies to all matter. All particles have an associated wavelength.
asks: Does wavelength depend on the particle?

faq.q: What is the difference between wave and particle behavior?
faq.a: Particles have definite positions like tiny balls. Waves spread out and interfere with each other.
asks: How are waves different from particles?
Can something be both a wave and a particle?

faq.q: Why do we see diffraction in electron experiments?
faq.a: Diffraction occurs because the electrons are behaving like waves when they interact with the crystal structure.
asks: What causes the pattern in the lab?

faq.q: What does the equation λ = h/p tell us?
faq.a: It tells us that the wavelength is inversely proportional to the momentum. More momentum means shorter wavelength.
asks: If p increases, what happens to λ?

facts: The de Broglie hypothesis suggests matter exhibits wave-like properties.
The equation relating wavelength to momentum is λ equals h divided by p.
Electron diffraction experiments provide strong evidence for wave-particle duality.
Planck's constant (h) has a specific, fixed value in SI units.

quiz.say: If an electron has twice the momentum, what happens to its de Broglie wavelength?
quiz.why: Since wavelength is inversely proportional to momentum, doubling the momentum halves the wavelength.

wrong.0: The equation clearly shows that wavelength depends on momentum.
wrong.1: This suggests that any momentum causes no wave behavior.
wrong.3: This confuses the direct relationship between wavelength and momentum.

quiz.say: Which physical quantity is used in the de Broglie equation?
quiz.why: The equation explicitly uses momentum in the denominator, along with h.

wrong.1: Energy is related but momentum is the specific variable in the de Broglie equation.
wrong.2: While speed is part of momentum, the equation uses the combined term, momentum.
wrong.3: Mass is part of momentum, but the equation requires the product of mass and velocity.

quiz.say: A particle with a very small momentum will have a:
quiz.why: Because wavelength is inversely proportional to momentum, a small denominator results in a large value.

wrong.1: This incorrectly assumes a direct relationship between momentum and wavelength.
wrong.2: Zero momentum would imply infinite wavelength, not zero.
wrong.3: This ignores the effect of the particle's momentum on the final wavelength.
